problem:
$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨\text{_______},\,y,\,({y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(y,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x={y}^{3}-{y}^{4}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [0,1].$ What is the first component of $r?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Surface of Revolution: Rotation About the y-Axis or z-Axis
examples.problem: The vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(y,\theta)$ parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x=1-\cos{y}$ by $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis for $y \in [0, \pi].$ What is $\mathbf{r}?$
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/be6fb27c0d050a7007e9f4a0d526daaff40b8f7d01f20c63ac8cc00074121f28.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $x=f(y)$ by $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,y\in [a,b],\,\theta =[0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $x=f(y) = 1-\cos{y} \geq 0$ for all $y \in [0, \pi].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\mathbf{r}(y,\theta) = 
\big\langle (1-\cos{y}) \cos\theta, \: 
y, \: 
(1-\cos{y}) \sin\theta 
\big\rangle,
\quad
y \in[0, \pi],
\quad
\theta \in [0,2\pi).
$$

feedback.problem: The vector-valued function $r(x,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [2,5].$ Which of the following could be $r?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/56a380b075d10862170ed9c9a45c07dddff3eaef1ea9fb3109a61cc3d27b5ac4.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [a,b]$ has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)\ge 0$ for all $x\in [2,5].$ 

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is 

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [2,5],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
